item.title: Agentic Software Engineering Bootcamp Day 1: From Spec to Production-Ready Software
item.abstract: Your AI assistant wrote the feature. The tests pass. It looks correct. But you didn't read every line, so how do you know it does what you meant? Maybe the model got it right the first time. Maybe not. From where you sit, those two outcomes look identical. That uncertainty, not the quality of any one tool, is the real distance between "I built something" and "I can put this in production."This hands-on, two-day workshop closes that distance. Day one is about aim: build fast and loose, hit the moment the assistant confidently produces something other than what you intended, and learn that the specification, not the code, was always the hard part. You'll leave with an app that does what you actually meant.Day two is about confidence. You'll build your own pre-commit checks for quality, security, dependency vulnerabilities, and your own design standards, and wire them into a gate that blocks bad commits across the whole codebase.For developers who already code with AI and want to move from "it works on my machine" to "I'd put my name on this." Bring a laptop and the AI tool you already use.

item.title: Workshop: Intentional API Design: Build APIs that Deliver Value to Humans and AI Agents
item.abstract:
Design APIs that truly serve their purpose — deliberately and effectively. In this workshop, you'll learn how to design APIs not just correctly, but intentionally — with a strong focus on stakeholder needs (AI agents and humans), usability, and long-term maintainability. Move beyond ad-hoc decisions and start crafting APIs as products that offer real value to both internal and external consumers.
Modern software architecture increasingly relies on well-designed APIs. Yet, too often, APIs are built without a clear understanding of who uses them, what they expect, and how design decisions affect long-term usability and maintenance. This workshop addresses the gap between building APIs right and building the right APIs. We explore the philosophy of Intentional API Design — the practice of making every design decision consciously and deliberately. You’ll learn to approach APIs not as mere technical interfaces, but as products shaped by business needs, user expectations, and architectural constraints.
Workshop Outline Block 1: Understanding API Stakeholders and Their Needs (AI Agents as a Stakeholder) Block 2: Intentional Design Principles Block 3: Frontend and Backend API Design Block 4: API Lifecycle and Iteration

item.title: Harness First: Turning LLMs into Production-Ready Agents
item.abstract: A model alone does not make an agent. To solve real problems reliably, the model needs a harness around it: tools, memory, context, workflows, guardrails, observability, and evaluation loops that shape how it reasons and acts. In this hands-on workshop, participants will start with a base LLM and progressively turn it into a production-ready agent by designing the surrounding system. We will cover how to define the agent’s task boundaries, connect tools and data sources, structure prompts and outputs, add human-in-the-loop controls, and align the agent’s behavior with the intended business goal. The second half of the workshop focuses on evaluation and iteration. Participants will learn how to build golden test sets, evaluate action paths, identify failure modes, debug unreliable behavior, and improve the harness through targeted changes rather than random prompt tweaking.By the end, attendees will understand how to move beyond “it worked in the demo” and build agents that can be tested, aligned, monitored, and improved over time.

item.title: AI Product Validation Day - From Idea to Validation
item.abstract: This hands-on workshop focuses on how to avoid wasted engineering cycles, de-risk decisions, and determine what is actually worth building before you commit resources. item.title: The Augmented Engineer [Onsite Only]
item.abstract: Most engineers have used AI to write code. Far fewer have used it for the work that actually fills their week like designing systems, pressure-testing assumptions, navigating incidents, synthesizing decisions, understanding unfamiliar codebases, and keeping institutional knowledge from evaporating into Slack threads. This full-day, hands-on workshop teaches software engineers and adjacent roles how to use AI as an adversarial thinking partner across the full range of engineering work. Participants learn to make AI argue against their designs, surface what they missed in a plan, find the root cause hiding behind a red herring, triage communication noise, and build reusable workflows that stick beyond the workshop itself. The day runs over a dozen blocks covering agent setup, context artifact creation, communication and connector workflows, visual design, research and decision-making, code review and threat modeling, incident response, documentation, and team evaluation — culminating in on-demand dashboards that surface how a team's time and effort is actually being spent. All instruction is tool-agnostic. Participants bring their own AI tool. The majority of each block is hands-on practice on realistic scenarios, with three consistent debrief questions that build the habit of treating AI output as a starting point, not an answer.

item.title: The Terminal is Your Canvas: Professional Vibe Coding with Claude Code
item.abstract: Forget copy-pasting from a browser tab. If you’re still using Claude through a standard chat window, you’re leaving massive velocity on the table.Claude Code brings Anthropic’s most powerful models directly into the terminal, executing complex, multi-step tasks natively inside a codebase or project directory. But going from "cool tool" to a predictable, production-grade workflow requires strategy.This intensive, one-day training is built for anyone who wants to master autonomous orchestration, safely manage multi-file mutations, and scale their output without losing control. While designed with software engineering patterns, this training is highly accessible to non-engineers with a strong technical foundation (e.g., technical product managers, solutions architects, data analysts, or technical founders) looking to bridge the gap between idea and execution.The Ultimate Claude MasterclassThis isn't a surface-level overview. By the end of this intensive day, you will know everything there is to know about Claude. From its underlying cognitive architecture and advanced prompting behaviors to its deepest terminal configurations, hidden flags, and agentic limits—you will leave with a complete, 360-degree understanding of Anthropic's ecosystem.Key Skills You Will Master:Agentic Orchestration: Directing autonomous AI agents to perform multi-step, multi-file operations safely.Context Engineering: Structuring project documentation and constraints so AI tools perfectly understand your domain.Workflow Automation: Building reusable custom skills, slash commands, and automated CI/CD pipelines.Modern Git Topology: Managing isolated development branches using Git worktrees to run parallel AI sessions without breaking your main workspace.Ecosystem Integration: Connecting LLMs to external data sources, APIs, and local developer tools using the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

item.title: Build Your Own MCP Server and Develop AI Agents from Scratch
item.abstract: In this full-day hands-on workshop, participants learn how to develop their own MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and use them to build powerful AI agents that can access external tools and data sources. From the basics of the MCP protocol to production-ready implementation—with plenty of hands-on experience and real-world use cases. Participants will gain in-depth insights into the architecture of the Model Context Protocol and develop their own MCP servers step by step. Through practical exercises and realistic scenarios, they will learn how to create AI agents that can interact seamlessly with different systems and data sources.
